sources.citation: Glottolog languoid page and reference records for Ham [hama1241] (refs 314356 Dobiyo 2001; 62231 Melis 2006; 111472 Ajello, Karyo, Melis & Dobio 2001; 580116 Gaffuri, Melis & Petrarca 2019).
sources.note: Bibliography only; Glottolog's most extensive description for Ham is Dobiyo 2001 'Esquisse phonologique du Ham' (MA, Universite de N'Djamena), typed 'phonology'.

sources.citation: Melis, Antonino & Suzy Platiel. 1998. Le statut du ton bas en masa (Tchad). Faits de langues 11-12. (Persee page flang_1244-5460_1998_num_6_11_1227, read online.)
sources.note: About Masa [mcn], not Ham; page text has no hit for Ham or accent. Not a Ham source.

sources.citation: De Dominicis, Amedeo. 2010. Tones and intonation in Gizey. Author's final draft deposited in Tuscia University Open Archive (hdl 2067/1373), CC BY-NC-ND.
sources.note: About Gizey (a tonal language), not Ham. Ham appears only in the classification sentence on p. 1 ('Masa (Masa, Gizey) and Musey (Musey, Ham, Marba-Lew, Monogoy)') and in the bibliography entry for Melis 2006/2007. Nothing on Ham stress or tone.

sources.citation: De Dominicis, Amedeo (ed.). 2007 [2006]. Undescribed and Endangered Languages: the Preservation of Linguistic Diversity. Newcastle: Cambridge Scholars Press. File deposited under the 'Introduction' record in Tuscia DSpace (hdl 2067/1392) -- a contents sheet only.
sources.note: Contents sheet only: confirms the chapter 'Ham: Une Langue et Une Culture en Danger de Disparition (Tchad)', Antonino Melis, Universite de N'Djamena; no chapter text, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Shryock, Aaron. 1997. The classification of the Masa group of languages. Studies in African Linguistics 26(1): 29-62.
